explanation: Sort durations increasingly. A duration at sorted index i contributes to the wait of exactly n−i−1 later queries, so sum duration×(n−i−1). Swapping an adjacent inverted pair decreases waiting by their duration difference.
timeComplexity: O(n log n) Sorting dominates the single linear contribution scan.
spaceComplexity: O(n) for sorting C#/JavaScript allocate a sorted copy; Python/Java sorting can use O(n) temporary storage, C++ copies its by-value argument.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/MinimumWaitingTime.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: Consider two adjacent tasks of durations a>b. Scheduling a first makes the second wait a, while swapping them makes the second wait only b; later waits are unchanged. Repeatedly removing such inversions proves increasing duration order minimizes total waiting. The accumulated elapsed time is each query’s actual wait.
walkthrough: For [6,1,3], sort to [1,3,6]. The contributions are 1×2, 3×1 and 6×0, totaling 5. These equal the waits 0,1,4.
edgeCases: The query’s own processing time is excluded from its wait.
Equal durations may be ordered arbitrarily.
